title: LUCas: Light-Uncaged Cas13a using photocleavable interfering guide RNAs.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Dryad application programming interface (API) record and landing page: the deposit is exactly 2 files, lucas-paper-code-v2.0.zip (166.3 MB) and README.md (43.7 KB), total 166.36 MB. I read the full README rendered on the landing page, which gives the directory tree, every config file, every raw plate-reader workbook, and the column-suffix conventions for the processed tables. Direct file download (API /files/<id>/download and /downloads/file_stream/<id>) returned 401 and 403 because Dryad now sits behind a bearer-token API and an anti-bot proof-of-work challenge; a ranged GET to read the zip's internal file list was also intercepted. The zip is in any case 166 MB, over the 50 MB download cap, so only metadata was recorded.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Row counts, replicate structure and the number of distinct guides come from the paper's figure legends and methods (all measurements in triplicate, n = 3 wells; 384-well plate reader; guides 9T-pc-igRNA, 19T-pc-igRNA 1 (cr4), cr6, cr7, 20T) and from the README's inventory of 13 configuration files and roughly 15 raw workbooks. I did not count a single row in any file.

a1_downloadable.note: Public Dryad deposit, no login and no access application; but the 166 MB zip exceeds the 50 MB cap and Dryad's anti-bot challenge blocked automated retrieval here, so the files were never opened.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: README states processed tables carry fitted reaction rates, suppression factors and limit-of-detection summaries as columns (*_reaction_rate_data.csv, *_suppression_factors.csv); taken from the README, not seen in a file.

a3_inputs_present.note: For any sequence-to-activity task the guide RNA sequences live only in the supplementary PDF's oligo table, not in a data column, and there are only about five distinct guides in the whole study.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are explicit in paper and README: cleaved reporter concentration in nM after fluorescence calibration, target in copies per microlitre, light dose in energy per second times exposure.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAILS. Everything is n = 3 replicate wells across roughly 15 plate experiments and about five guides; distinct independent conditions are on the order of tens, far under the 1,500-row bar. No row count verified.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 166 MB zip; processed CSV tables far smaller
a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially laptop-sized; only the 50 MB project cap, not RAM, stopped the download.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not checkable: no row counts published and no file opened, but the README's inventory matches the paper's six figures one-for-one.

a8_label_provenance.note: Rates are least-squares fits to measured fluorescence, so they trace to a physical measurement; however much of the deposit is ordinary differential equation simulation output, which is model output and unusable as a label.

existing_models.name: ADAPT (Metsky et al., 'Designing sensitive viral diagnostics with machine learning', Nature Biotechnology 2022)
existing_models.score_and_split: Search result reports Spearman correlation 0.69-0.84 for ranking candidate Cas13a guides across internal and external validation, over assays spanning 1,933 vertebrate-infecting viruses; I read the search summary, not the paper.

existing_models.name: TIGER ('Prediction of on-target and off-target activity of CRISPR-Cas13d guide RNAs using deep learning', Nature Biotechnology 2023)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved beyond title; covers Cas13d guide on- and off-target activity, a different enzyme from the LbuCas13a used here.

existing_models.name: Dual-branch neural network for Cas13a guide activity ('Accurate Prediction of CRISPR/Cas13a Guide Activity Using Feature Selection and Deep Learning', J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2025)
existing_models.score_and_split: Search summary states it beats sequence-only models on two independent Cas13a datasets using 99 selected descriptive features; numbers not retrieved.

backbone.name: None appropriate; RNA-FM (an RNA language model) would be the candidate for guide sequences, but there are only about five guide sequences here.
backbone.hardware: CPU would suffice, but there is nothing to embed.
backbone.licence: Dryad deposit is open (Creative Commons); paper is CC-BY 4.0.

integration.partner_dataset: ADAPT's Cas13a guide activity screens or the published Cas13a/Cas12a kinetic parameter compilation (Analytical Chemistry 2022, 50 sets of rate parameters).
integration.join_key: guide RNA sequence / enzyme ortholog name
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Could not write one that this data supports: with about five guides it adds a handful of rows to any cross-study kinetic table, which changes no conclusion.

controls.positive_control: Reaction rate must rise monotonically with target concentration and with ultraviolet dose, which the authors already show directly.
controls.negative_control: No-target control and no-ribonucleoprotein wells are present in the raw plates.
controls.external_validation: The deposit includes a comparison to Ramachandran et al.'s published analytical and numerical reporter-cleavage model, so one published curve could be reproduced.

honest_claim_h3: Any model trained on this deposit could only claim 'we can re-estimate the trans-cleavage rate of one Cas13a enzyme with about five guide designs under one lab's buffer and plate-reader conditions', which the authors' own ordinary differential equation model already does mechanistically.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use fluorescence-over-time curves from a light-triggered CRISPR test to predict how much target RNA was in the tube.
plain_idea.train_on: Each example would be one well of a 384-well plate: a calibrated time series of cleaved reporter concentration before and after a brief ultraviolet flash, plus the guide used and the reaction matrix (water, plasma, or amplified). The number of wells is unknown; the paper reports triplicates across roughly 15 plate experiments and about five guides, so likely a few hundred.
plain_idea.predict: Target RNA concentration in copies per microlitre (or simply target present versus absent). The truth is the experimenter's own spike-in concentration, made by serial dilution of in-vitro-transcribed RNA.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Point-of-care CRISPR diagnostics teams would like to read concentration off an early, noisy curve rather than waiting 60 minutes; even a negative result would show that a two-phase mechanistic rate fit cannot be beaten by a learned read-out.

more_or_better_data.why: ADAPT was trained on guide activity screens covering 1,933 viruses; this deposit has roughly five guide designs for one enzyme (LbuCas13a) in one lab. The only thing it covers that they do not is photocleavable caging, and it covers that with a handful of conditions.

confidence_score.why: Triplicate wells and propagated fit uncertainty do give a genuine noise estimate per rate, which sequence-based guide predictors do not report; but three replicates per condition over tens of conditions is too thin to calibrate a model.

models_beatable.why: The relevant competitor here is not a machine-learning model at all but the authors' own two-phase Michaelis-Menten and ordinary differential equation fits, which already predict the limit of detection and were validated experimentally in this paper.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails on every condition: the existing predictors take guide sequence as input and are not runnable on these time series, the assays differ, and there is no shared evaluation split.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: learn target RNA concentration (or simply target presence) from the shape of the pre- and post-illumination fluorescence time series of a light-uncaged Cas13a reaction, so a result could be called early. Dies on sample size: a few hundred wells that collapse to tens of independent guide-by-concentration conditions, and a mechanistic rate fit that the authors already show works.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from the Dryad size record (166.36 MB total) and the README's description of long-form CSV tables; nothing was downloaded or timed because the zip exceeds the 50 MB cap and Dryad blocked automated download.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Open data/processed/*_reaction_rate_data.csv and count distinct guide-by-target-concentration conditions (not wells, not time points). If that number is in the tens, as the paper's n = 3 figure legends imply, stop.

verdict_reason: Fails A5 on independent sample size. This is an assay-engineering paper: every measurement is n = 3 replicate wells across roughly 15 plate-reader experiments and about five photocleavable guide designs for one enzyme, so the number of independent examples is in the tens, not the 1,500 the checklist requires. It also fails A3 for any sequence-to-activity framing, because the guide sequences appear only in a supplementary PDF and there are only about five of them. The quantity a model would predict (trans-cleavage rate, limit of detection) is already predicted well by the authors' own mechanistic two-phase kinetic and ordinary differential equation models, which they validate experimentally, so machine learning is not the right tool here (checklist I4). Secondary, non-fatal note: the data is openly deposited but the 166 MB zip exceeds the 50 MB cap and Dryad's anti-bot challenge blocked automated download, so no file was opened.
